overall: Tomorrow (Tuesday, June 23) is expected to be a mostly sunny, post-frontal day for Atlanta following a round of heavy overnight thunderstorms (90% PoP tonight). A west wind around 10 mph with gusts to 25 mph will usher in somewhat cooler and drier air behind the departing system. Only a slight chance of lingering showers before 7 AM, with clearing skies and comfortable conditions through the afternoon.
forecast_obs_notes: Model agreement is poor and spread is wide: ECMWF (~81°F), GFS (~80°F), and HRRR (~82°F) form a tight NWP cluster in the low 80s, while NBM (~86°F) and the NWS text forecast (near 86°F) sit notably higher; WEATHER_COM (~83°F) falls in between, and the full obs-adjusted ensemble model lands at just 79.2°F — suggesting significant uncertainty and a likely overestimate from NBM/NWS relative to the dynamical models.
max_temp_prediction: The dominant signal from the major NWP models (ECMWF, GFS, HRRR) clusters around 80–82°F, consistent with post-frontal west flow and overnight storm passage cooling the airmass from today's 91.4°F observed high. The NWS text and NBM are bullish at 86°F but appear to underestimate the degree of post-frontal cooling, while the full ensemble's 79.2°F may be slightly too aggressive. Confidence is low (Tier 4 per both bucket sets), but the best estimate centers near 82°F with a plausible range of roughly 79–86°F.
